lines.speaker: me
lines.text: For the setup it's a one-off 1,500, and then 425 a month after that.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Oof. Yeah, to be honest that's quite a bit more than I expected.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: That feels pretty expensive for what it is.

expect: Does not defend the price, but asks what the customer compares it with or what the problem costs them each month now.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: So if you put it all together, you end up at 425 a month.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Hmm. Okay.

expect: Lets the silence after the price sit and adds nothing, or at most asks a short open question such as 'How does that sound to you?'.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Then you're at 425 a month, and you can cancel every quarter.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Okay. And if we sign up for a full year right away, can you knock something off?

expect: Does not give a discount straight away, but first checks whether the rest of the proposal fits, or offers a smaller start instead of a lower price.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: So the first step would be a four-week pilot.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yeah. Yeah, I get it.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: I think I just need to think it over a bit.

expect: Asks in a friendly way what exactly the customer still wants to think over, so the real objection (price, trust or someone else) comes out.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: You know what, let me sleep on it.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: I'll get back to you sometime next week.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Sure, of course.

expect: Sets a concrete date for the follow-up right now and asks what is still in the way.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Shall I quickly show you what that would look like for you?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: No, you know what, just email me some information first.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Then I can take a look in my own time.

expect: Agrees, but asks what exactly the customer wants to see to move forward, and books a follow-up right away.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: If you like, we could start as soon as next month.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yeah, sounds good, but I really have to run this past my business partner first.

expect: Asks what the partner will want to know or push back on, and offers to join that conversation.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Personally I think it's a good plan.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: But something like this has to go past the board, I can't decide that on my own.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Yeah, makes sense.

expect: Asks what the board needs to say yes, and offers a short summary or a joint call.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: We take the whole lead follow-up off your hands.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Right, but to be honest we just do that ourselves now. Our sales team calls everyone back.

expect: Asks how well that works now and how many hours a week it costs the sales team, without knocking their approach.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: I've got a nephew who's pretty handy with that kind of stuff.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: I reckon he could put something like that together too, right?

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Yeah, he might.

expect: Acknowledges that and asks who maintains it when something breaks, and what it costs if it is down for a week.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: We actually already work with a marketing agency.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: They do some automation stuff as well, I think.

expect: Asks how happy they are with that and what is still left undone, without knocking the other agency.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: How is that set up for you at the moment?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Well, we have a regular IT company, they basically do everything for us.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: So I'm not sure we want another supplier on top of that.

expect: Positions the service as an addition that takes work off their plate, and asks what the IT company does not pick up now.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Look, last year we had something like this built as well.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Cost us a few thousand and in the end nobody used it.

expect: Names that they got burned (a label), asks what went wrong back then and what has to be different now.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Honestly, I'm a bit fed up with all these AI promises.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Everyone says it solves everything and then it always disappoints.

expect: Acknowledges the doubt with a label and suggests starting small with a result that can be measured.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: It sounds interesting, but now really isn't a good time.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: We're right in the middle of our busy season, maybe after the summer.

expect: Asks what will be different after the summer and what each month of waiting costs now.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Roughly when would you want to get started?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Phew, probably not until next year. We still have to roll out our new CRM first.

expect: Asks when the CRM goes live and whether it would be smart to include the automation in that, and books a follow-up moment.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yeah, but does this actually work?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Because on paper everything sounds great, of course.

expect: Mentions a concrete result from the profile or suggests a small pilot with a clear measure of success, without making anything up.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Have you done this before for a company like ours?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: A trades business, I mean, with engineers out on the road.

expect: Only mentions a matching case if it is in the profile, otherwise says honestly that the user will check, plus a question about their situation.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: So where does all that data about our customers actually end up?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Because with GDPR we really have to be careful about that.

expect: Only gives an answer that is in the profile (such as a data processing agreement or storage in the EU), and otherwise has the user promise to find out and email it.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Our lawyer is going to look at this either way.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Mostly at the AI part. Do you train on our data or something?

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Good question.

expect: Promises nothing that is not in the profile, offers to send the details in writing to the lawyer and asks what exactly they want to see.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: That's how it works, in short.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Okay, clear. How soon could we actually get started?

expect: Assumes the sale and suggests a concrete start date or first step, for example a choice between two dates.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Say we go ahead, what would you need from us to get started?

expect: Names the first step briefly and moves toward the decision, for example who should be at the kickoff and when.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Does this work with HubSpot too? Because that's where all our customer data lives.

expect: Gives the answer if it is in the profile, and otherwise has the user say they will check and email it today.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: And how long does it take before it's all up and running?

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Uh, let me see.

expect: Gives the lead time from the profile in one sentence, or has the user promise to check exactly and email it.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Good morning! How's your day going so far?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yeah, fine, thanks. Awful weather out there though, it's been raining all morning again.

expect: Answers PASS: ordinary small talk with no objection, buying signal or question.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Hang on, I can't hear you very well.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Let me sort out my headphones. There we go, can you hear me now?

expect: Answers PASS: technical chat about the connection, the question is not a sales question.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Did you get away at all this summer?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yeah, two weeks in France with the kids. It was lovely, but now it's straight back to full speed.

expect: Answers PASS: personal small talk at the start of the call.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Sorry I'm a few minutes late, my last meeting ran over a bit.

expect: Answers PASS: an apology before the start, not a moment for a tip.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: Hi Sandra, good to finally catch you.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yeah, I'm in the car right now, so I've got you on speaker.

expect: Answers PASS: a practical remark with no objection or buying signal.

lines.speaker: me
lines.text: And then those requests land in your shared inbox automatically.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Yeah, okay, I'm still with you.

expect: Answers PASS: neutral agreement during the explanation, nothing to react to.
